<p>“Na-hyeon, if the Association contacts you, just say what we agreed on. And if anything happens, call me right away, got it?”</p><p>“You worry too much. Go have fun with Ji-hyeon.”</p><p>“Yeah.”</p><p>Before leaving with Ji-hyeon, I explained the situation to Na-hyeon, but my feet wouldn’t move. Anxiety kept me repeating myself over and over.</p><p>“No, if the Association calls, don’t answer—just contact me first.”</p><p>“Oppa, give me the car keys. I’ll get in first.”</p><p>“Alright. Let’s go…”</p><p>With Yu-na and Na-hyeon smiling as they saw me off, and Echo staring at me with a bored, indifferent expression, Ji-hyeon and I finally left the house.</p><p>After getting in the car, we headed to the bustling downtown area near Ji-hyeon’s university.</p><p>“But how do I even prove I’m her brother? It’s not like I’m carrying a family registry certificate…”</p><p>“Maybe they’ll just believe it when they see us in person?”</p><p>I knew from the community forums that siblings often didn’t get along, but it still felt surreal that people genuinely didn’t believe in the existence of a caring older brother.</p><p>‘Even if they don’t have a relationship like Ji-hyeon and me… wouldn’t they at least pick up their little sister if she’s drunk?’</p><p>What if it were a little brother instead?</p><p>‘If it’s a guy… well, he should handle it himself…’</p><p>It was discriminatory, but there was nothing I could do about it. How could the treatment of sisters and brothers ever be the same?</p><p>***</p><p>“There’s quite a crowd.”</p><p>Even though I’d been to this university district with Ji-hyeon before, every time I came, it felt vibrant and overflowing with youthful energy.</p><p>People in their early twenties and couples strolled down the street, radiating vitality.</p><p>‘Wait, I’m still in my early twenties too…’</p><p>If I hadn’t become a Hunter, maybe I’d be living an ordinary life like this.</p><p>“Hey! Ji-hyeon!”</p><p>“Ji-hyeon-ah!”</p><p>“Huh?”</p><p>Ji-hyeon waved back at a woman in the distance who was calling out to her.</p><p>As we got closer, the woman—who seemed to be Ji-hyeon’s friend—bowed her head in greeting.</p><p><img src="data:image/webp;base64," alt="291096" loading="lazy">
</p><p>“Hello! You must be Ji-hyeon’s oppa, right?”</p><p>“Yes, nice to meet you.”</p><p>“Oppa, she’s my classmate. Her name is Jeong Ji-hyeon. Isn’t it funny that we’re both named Ji-hyeon?”</p><p>“Yeah.”</p><p>Ji-hyeon wasn’t an uncommon name, so it wasn’t all that surprising, but it still felt a little odd that we were both calling each other Ji-hyeon.</p><p>“So, should we go in?”</p><p>“Sure!”</p><p>Naturally, since I was the one paying for the drinks, I told her to pick wherever she wanted to eat. I figured she’d go for some expensive place since it was free, but to my surprise, she chose a pretty ordinary bar.</p><p>The only difference from other bars was that it was a room-style place where every table was in a private booth.</p><p>After we sat down, we ordered some snacks and started drinking in earnest. As expected of college students, they had a bold side to them.</p><p>Even though it was our first meeting, they immediately filled their glasses, shouted “Cheers!” with enthusiasm, and downed their soju. Watching them, I couldn’t help but laugh.</p><p>“Are you really Ji-hyeon’s oppa?”</p><p>“Yeah, biologically and legally, she’s my little sister.”</p><p>“See? I told you! Look closely—don’t we look a lot alike?”</p><p>“Hmm… I can’t really tell…”</p><p>That made sense. The women in our family had all inherited Yu-na’s strong beauty genes, so they were all stunning. But if I looked in the mirror and judged my own face…</p><p>‘Average…? Or maybe just a little above average…?’</p><p>They say sons take after their mothers and daughters after their fathers, but that didn’t seem to apply to our family. In fact, my dad and I didn’t look alike at all—except for the fact that we were both male.</p><p>My dad had been short with sharp features, while I was the complete opposite in build.</p><p>“Look at this!”</p><p>“Is this you, Ji-hyeon? You were so cute back then, what’s wrong with you now?”</p><p>“Where… did you get this?”</p><p>“From Mom.”</p><p>Ji-hyeon pulled up a photo on her phone and showed it to us. It was a picture of three very young siblings holding hands.</p><p>“Mom said this was the last photo we took together before we all started living apart.”</p><p>Jung Ji-hyeon finally seemed convinced and silently nodded.</p><p>“Now do you believe me?”</p><p>“I have no choice but to. Fine, I believe you. And oppa, please speak comfortably with me.”</p><p>“Got it.”</p><p>Honestly, I got the feeling that proving I was her brother was just an excuse—she probably just wanted to hang out with me.</p><p>***</p><p>“Oppa…”</p><p>“I knew this would happen.”</p><p>How much had they drunk? From the first bar, Ji-hyeon had been happily chugging away until she got completely wasted. Meanwhile, Jeong Ji-hyeon had clearly drunk just as much, yet she didn’t seem drunk at all.</p><p>‘She can really hold her liquor.’</p><p>“Ji-hyeon, are you okay? Want to go to the bathroom?”</p><p>“No… more… drink…”</p><p>“….”</p><p>Jeong Ji-hyeon shook Ji-hyeon awake with a worried expression, but Ji-hyeon just mumbled incoherently, her face planted on the table.</p><p>“Ji-hyeon’s really drunk.”</p><p>“Yeah, I should call a taxi.”</p><p>After ordering a taxi on his phone, he finished paying the bill and helped Ji-hyeon out of the bar, supporting her weight.</p><p>“I’ll drop you off somewhere close to your place. Ride with us.”</p><p>“Ji-hyeon’s place is nearby, so we can just get off together.”</p><p>With Ji-hyeon leaning on him, the three of them took the taxi and got off near her apartment.</p><p>“I’m worried about Ji-hyeon, so I’ll go up to her room with you.”</p><p>“Huh?”</p><p>He’d assumed they’d part ways after getting out of the taxi, but Jeong Ji-hyeon ruffled Ji-hyeon’s hair and, still supporting her, followed them up to Ji-hyeon’s room.</p><p>Even if she was a good drinker, Jeong Ji-hyeon had to have downed nearly three bottles of soju, yet her complexion hadn’t changed at all—she looked perfectly fine.</p><p>As an Awakened, I could chug soju like it was water and feel no different, but Jeong Ji-hyeon was just a normal person.</p><p>‘Wait…’</p><p>“Hnnng…”</p><p>After tossing Ji-hyeon onto the bed, Jeong Ji-hyeon started undressing her and tidying up various things.</p><p>“Ah…”</p><p>Now I understood why Jeong Ji-hyeon had come up with us.</p><p>My family’s relationships were definitely abnormal. I’d never felt dissatisfaction or doubt about it, but if outsiders found out, it would without a doubt cause a huge scandal. That’s why it made sense to keep it a strict secret.</p><p>So… if I had brought Ji-hyeon back to her room alone, I would’ve casually undressed her, and if necessary, even helped her bathe without a second thought.</p><p>‘That would’ve been weird…’</p><p>But from an outsider’s perspective, no matter how close siblings were, they wouldn’t go that far for each other.</p><p>Probably… Jeong Ji-hyeon had followed us to handle the aftermath, worried I might be in an awkward position.</p><p>“Is Hunter life tough?”</p><p>“Uh… what? How’d you know?”</p><p>After putting Ji-hyeon to bed, Jeong Ji-hyeon sat in a chair, sipping water, and asked me.</p><p>“How wouldn’t I know? Last time, Ji-hyeon got drunk while drinking with me and spilled the beans.”</p><p>“…”</p><p>“And didn’t you know that Hunters ranked A or higher have their information publicly available? Even if their photos and detailed personal info aren’t disclosed, anyone can look up an A-rank Hunter.”</p><p>“Ah…”</p><p>I had known that fact, but back then, becoming an A-rank Hunter had felt like such a distant dream that I’d forgotten all about it.</p><p>“Well… I just take on the safest jobs I can find and handle them.”</p><p>“I dropped out of the Hunter Training Academy.”</p><p>“What?”</p><p>“Didn’t you notice? I’m an Awakened too. Not that I had any standout Abilities—even if I’d graduated, I’d have been lucky to make it to D-rank.”</p><p>So that explained why Jeong Ji-hyeon could drink so much without getting drunk—she was an Awakened.</p><p>It wasn’t uncommon for trainees to leave the academy. Some Awakened had bodies far stronger and healthier than ordinary people, yet still fell short of true Hunter standards. They often lived ordinary lives, hovering between the line of normal humans and superhumans.</p><p>Even simple manual labor would be far more efficient for them—they wouldn’t tire easily, their health wouldn’t suffer, so at the very least, they’d never go hungry.</p><p>‘Well… Awakened college students aren’t that unusual either…’</p><p>“Sometimes I wonder… If I hadn’t dropped out, would I be a Hunter by now? Or would I still be in training?”</p><p>“If it doesn’t suit you, leaving was the right call.”</p><p>Before I knew it, I was sitting across from Jeong Ji-hyeon, listening intently to her story.</p><p>Perhaps pleased to have found someone who understood her situation, she began to open up, speaking candidly about her past.</p><p>She seemed well-versed in the Hunter world—the cutthroat competition at the academy, the harsh reality of E and D-rank Hunters who often ended up injured, retired, or dead. She knew it all.</p><p>“Wait… did you call me here because you wanted to meet a Hunter?”</p><p>“Yes, that was part of it. I did want to see an A-rank Hunter at least once.”</p><p>As I suspected. That cleared up one of the questions that had been nagging at me since yesterday.</p><p>It had always struck me as odd that she’d called me just to confirm whether her friend’s brother was really her blood brother. It seemed Jeong Ji-hyeon had simply wanted to meet a Hunter as a former trainee and talk.</p><p>“What was the other reason?”</p><p>“Because you’re my type.”</p><p>“Huh?”</p><p>Jeong Ji-hyeon stared at me without a hint of hesitation, her expression unchanging as she declared boldly,</p><p>“My brother’s a Hunter too… I told Ji-hyeon we weren’t close, but the truth is, my parents divorced when I was little. My brother emigrated and works as a Hunter overseas. We haven’t seen each other in so long that we’re neither close nor estranged. We’d have to meet in person to even argue…”</p><p>“···.”</p><p>“When we were kids, Ji-hyeon and I were as close as you and Seong-hyeon hyung. So when I saw you taking care of her at the bar that day, it reminded me of him. Maybe it was some kind of complex? I guess that’s what it was.”</p><p>She laid her feelings bare so honestly that I had no response.</p><p>“Would you like to go out with me?”</p><p>And then, are all college students this bold? Ji-hyeon’s direct, full-speed-ahead approach made me let out a hollow laugh.</p><p>“Dating my little sister’s friend is a bit…”</p><p>“Why? I’m pretty cute, aren’t I?”</p><p>“That’s not the issue.”</p><p>This was truly a bizarre scene. Ji-hyeon was passed out drunk in the bedroom, and here I was, sitting face-to-face in the living room with Ji-hyeon’s friend—also named Ji-hyeon—having a conversation.</p><p>Surprisingly, Yoon Ji-hyeon kept shifting topics and leading the conversation, so the awkwardness faded away.</p><p>As we talked, my guard must have completely dropped, because I ended up asking her something I’d been curious about.</p><p>“Actually, there’s something that’s been bothering me since earlier…”</p><p>“Hmm?”</p><p>“Your… tongue…”</p><p>There was something that had caught my eye the first time I saw Yoon Ji-hyeon.</p><p>And that was…</p><p>“Ah, this? I got it the day I turned twenty. Is it weird?”</p><p>Yoon Ji-hyeon opened her mouth and stuck out her tongue, revealing the silver piercing embedded in it.</p><p><img src="data:image/webp;base64," alt="291097" loading="lazy">
</p><p>“Y-You didn’t have to go that far…”</p><p>She was so aggressive in sticking her tongue out to show me that I was flustered. It was my first time seeing a tongue piercing, so I’d asked out of curiosity—but I hadn’t expected her to actually show me like this.</p><p>“What? If you’re curious, do you want to touch it?”</p><p>Yoon Ji-hyeon stood up from her chair, leaned in close, and stuck out her tongue again.</p><p>And just like that, the atmosphere in the room shifted into a familiar one.</p><p><img src="data:image/webp;base64," alt="291098" loading="lazy">
</p><p>‘This atmosphere…’</p><p>If I touched that piercing, it would definitely lead to at least a kiss.</p><p>But honestly… I kind of wanted to touch it.</p><p><img src="data:image/webp;base64," alt="291099" loading="lazy">
</p><p>“It’s fine, go ahead and touch it.”</p><p>“···.”</p>
